_comment: Disagreements between tools/oracle/recognizer.py and the reference parser on conformance cases. Each entry: class + note, PENDING AUTHOR DECISION. Empty since the author decisions of 2026-10-09 (D3 META fold fallback, D4 lexicographic priority, D5 line edges), which settled the classes meta-fold-fallback, priority-combination and surrounding-line-terminator.
_observations: Differential sweep after the author decisions of 2026-10-09 (not part of the corpus): every sequence of length 1-5 over {jan, ma, tan, li, e, la, pi, anu} (37448) plus 30000 random sequences of length 6-9 (seed 20261009), comparing status, skeleton set and span-free AST shape: 0 disagreements, 0 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The same sweep against the parser of commit 0f14b00 finds 61 disagreements, every one a META fold fallback on a sequence with a foldable run (that parser INVALID; oracle RESOLVED 57, AMBIGUOUS 4), so the sweep is not vacuous.

Settled classes: meta-fold-fallback (D3: a fold applies only where the reading is valid), priority-combination (D4: fold positions by inclusion, then structural-tan positions by inclusion), surrounding-line-terminator (D5: spaces/tabs and one final LF or CR LF are ignored; any other line boundary is INVALID). Cases: conformance/canon_2026_10_09.jsonl, amb2-meta-09, amb2-tan-01.

Interpretation shared by the oracle and the parser, for the author to confirm: D4 step 1 compares the sets of folded TOKEN POSITIONS. Comparing the sets of folded runs instead differs only where one run lies strictly inside an overlapping run of another unit, e.g. 'jan li tan ma tan ma tan ma': by positions ({jan} li {D2(tan ma)}) wins (positions 2-7 include 3-6); by run identity the two folds are incomparable and step 2 would pick ({jan} li tan {D1(ma tan) ma}).
